item.title: Election Officials Fear Federal Interference in Voting Next Week
item.description: State and local plans for Election Day include how to react to potential I.C.E. raids, misbehavior by federal election monitors and attempts to seize votes or machines.
item.dc:creator: Richard Fausset, Zolan Kanno-Youngs and David W. Chen
item.media:description: State and local election officials across the country have been redoubling training efforts to prepare for the potential for federal interference.

item.title: Joe Redner, the ‘Strip Club King’ of Tampa, Has Died
item.description: More than just the owner of an adult venue, Joe Redner was a political gadfly and fierce advocate for free speech and gay rights. He was 86.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:credit: Pendygraft/Tampa Bay Times, via ZUMA Press Wire
item.media:description: Joe Redner at his Mons Venus club in 2019. During his 50-year career in adult entertainment, Mr. Redner owned multiple strip clubs in and around Tampa, Fla.

item.title: A Tight Senate Race in Mississippi? Trump and Others Seem to Think So.
item.description: President Trump on Monday was the latest big political star to swing through Mississippi and boost a candidate in a red-state Senate race that suddenly seems competitive.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane
item.media:description: President Trump and Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith at a rally on Monday night in Corinth, Miss.

item.title: How Netanyahu Strained the U.S.-Israel Alliance
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s prime minister, has long sold himself as the best politician to manage relations with America. Our reporter Mark Mazzetti describes how that alliance is now under strain as support for Israel erodes across party lines.
item.dc:creator: Mark Mazzetti, Joy Sung, James Surdam and Pierre Kattar

item.title: Obama’s ‘Cheesecake Factory’ Jab Rankles Trump on Mississippi Campaign Stop
item.description: Former President Barack Obama had cast his successor as out of touch while jabbing at his extravagant sense of style. Mr. Trump responded at length.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:description: President Donald Trump during a campaign rally at the Crossroads Arena, in Corinth, Miss., on Monday.

item.title: Judge Temporarily Blocks Further Alterations at D.C.’s East Potomac Park
item.description: A federal judge stopped the Trump administration from cutting trees and prohibited other changes at the park where the president has sought to overhaul a golf course.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:description: Trees that have been cut down at East Potomac Golf Links are seen earlier this month in Washington. The Trump administration and the National Park Service moved to cut down up to 529 trees at East Potomac Golf Links.

item.title: El-Sayed Campaign Distances Itself From Group’s Ad Critical of Israel
item.description: As the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan seeks to overcome intraparty tensions, his opponent in the primary, Haley Stevens, said a PAC’s ad was “fearmongering about Israel.”
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dr. El-Sayed’s campaign said that the advertisement is “not affiliated in any way with the Abdul for Senate campaign.”

item.title: Bob Woodward Criticizes Jeff Bezos in New Memoir
item.description: Six takeaways from a new memoir by Mr. Woodward, the star Washington Post reporter, including his disappointment with the newspaper’s billionaire owner.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker
item.media:credit: Caroline Gutman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Bob Woodward has reported on Washington politics for more than half a century.

item.title: Appeals Court Declines to Intervene in California Ballot Lawsuit
item.description: By a 2-1 vote, a federal appeals court panel denied the Trump administration’s request that it immediately order the state to set aside 20,000 mail-in ballots.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: Ballots being processed in City of Industry, Calif., during last year’s election.

item.title: Ohio State Professor Who Tackled a Filmmaker on Campus Resigns
item.description: The professor, Luke M. Perez, taught at the university’s civics center. He wrestled down a documentary filmmaker who was trying to question the university’s former president.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Saul
item.media:description: Luke M. Perez, left, an Ohio State professor, appeared in court in February after he was charged with assaulting Mike Newman, far right, a documentary filmmaker.

item.title: Trump Dangles $1 Million Reward for Reporting Voter Fraud
item.description: It was unclear how the president would pay for the proposal, which fused his campaign trail promotion of financial incentives to help his party win and his unfounded warnings about voter fraud.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Pager
item.media:description: President Trump heading to a rally in Mississippi on Monday. He promised $1 million to anyone reporting voter fraud “upon the arrest and conviction” of the fraudsters.

item.title: The Other Dan Sullivan Fires Back at Trump’s Lawsuit in Alaska
item.description: Dan Sullivan, a schoolteacher, has the same name as a Republican senator in Alaska. He said that a pre-emptive lawsuit challenging the results was “a gross misuse of the Justice Department.”
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning
item.media:credit: Christopher Miller for The New York Times
item.media:description: Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., the retired teacher running for Senate, called the experience “unending stress” in an email exchange with The Alaska Beacon.

item.title: Justice Dept. Brings More Charges Against Comey, Accusing Him of Leaks
item.description: Lawyers for James B. Comey said the case centered on an issue that had already been investigated and had not led to charges, of a purported leak of national security information to The Times in October 2016.
item.dc:creator: Devlin Barrett
item.media:description: James B. Comey, the former F.B.I. director, testifying before the Senate Intelligence Committee in 2017.

item.title: Manhunt Begins After Convicted Murderer Escapes From Tennessee Prison
item.description: Jacob Allen Morley, 28, was discovered to be missing late Sunday at a correctional facility in Tiptonville, Tenn., officials said.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra E. Petri
item.media:description: Security footage showing an inmate, Jacob Allen Morley, who escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex on Sunday.

item.title: What Early Voting Can Reveal About the 2026 Midterm Elections So Far
item.description: Millions of early votes tell us less than many would think, but there are key takeaways from results in Texas, Kansas, Georgia and North Carolina.
item.dc:creator: Evan Reynolds
item.media:description: Voters waited in line to participate in early voting at the Marty Robbins Recreation Center in El Paso last week.

item.title: Teen Arrested in Florida Shooting Will Be Tried as Adult, Officials Say
item.description: The 15-year-old suspect will be charged with 11 counts of attempted second-degree murder after the shooting on Saturday that happened after Florida A&M’s homecoming game.
item.dc:creator: Billy Witz
item.media:credit: Alicia Devine/Tallahassee Democrat, via Imagn Images, via Reuters
item.media:description: The Tallahassee police at the scene of the shooting on Saturday, about an hour after Florida A&M University’s homecoming game.

item.title: Last Ditch, a Lesbian Bar Whose Mask Policy Made It Famous, Will Close
item.description: The Massachusetts bar, which catered to lesbians, lifted its Covid mask requirement once a week to attract more patrons. The decision brought criticism and national attention, but did not save the business.
item.dc:creator: Mark Arsenault
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: Some people were upset that the bar had lifted its mask policy one day a week, saying it risked the lives of immunocompromised customers. Others mocked them.

item.title: How Scuffles at Trump Rallies Echo His Past Events
item.description: Examining President Trump’s praise of a rallygoer who punched a protester last week, David E. Sanger, a White House and national security correspondent for The New York Times, studied the atmosphere at Mr. Trump’s recent events. What he found was a faint echo of the moments that made Mr. Trump’s 2016 rallies so shocking.
item.dc:creator: David E. Sanger, Gilad Thaler, Nour Idriss, Nikolay Nikolov and Pierre Kattar

item.title: Former South Carolina Governors Endorse Annie Andrews Over Darline Graham in Senate Race
item.description: Former Republican Gov. David Beasley and Democratic Gov. Jim Hodges recorded a joint video throwing their support to the Democrat in the tight Senate race.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.media:credit: Sean Rayford for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dr. Annie Andrews, the Democrat running against Senator Darline Graham, was endorsed by two former South Carolina governors.

item.title: House Democrats Call for Special Counsel to Scrutinize Trump’s Ties to Epstein
item.description: The request comes as Democrats are working to paint Republicans as corrupt and highlight their plans to investigate Trump should they win the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:description: President Trump has repeatedly denied any involvement in or knowledge of Jeffrey Epstein’s sex-trafficking operation.

item.title: Swing State Republican in a Razor-Thin Race Tries to Outrun Trump
item.description: Joe Lombardo, the governor of Nevada, was favored to win a second term. Now he’s in one of the nation’s tightest contests.
item.dc:creator: Reis Thebault and Sejal Govindarao
item.media:credit: Emily Najera for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gov. Joe Lombardo of Nevada is considered one of the most vulnerable Republican candidates for governor this election cycle.

item.title: Ken Paxton’s State-Funded Jet-Setting Draws Campaign Scrutiny
item.description: Mr. Paxton, the Republican candidate for Senate in Texas, has taken about 350 trips outside of the state since he was sworn in as attorney general.
item.dc:creator: Beth Reinhard and Lauren McGaughy
item.media:description: Ken Paxton attending a campaign rally with President Trump earlier this month.

item.title: In Maine, an ‘Oyster Thug’s’ Struggle to Get Over Graham Platner
item.description: A Platner superfan’s reluctance to support the Democrat now running against Senator Susan Collins reflects the party’s challenges navigating left-wing passions.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Williamson
item.media:credit: Ryan David Brown for The New York Times

item.title: The Storm Wrecked Their Bridges. ‘All That Red Tape’ Left Them Stranded.
item.description: Hundreds of households in North Carolina remain without a private bridge two years after Hurricane Helene. Many are frustrated by a state program’s progress.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Medina and Allison Joyce

item.title: What to Know About Trump’s Rally in Mississippi
item.description: President Trump will stump for a senator in a state he has won three times by double digits, and as Democrats see a path to victory.
item.dc:creator: John Yoon
item.media:description: President Trump will travel to Mississippi on Monday to campaign for Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith.
